sources.title: Other countries: historical records guide
sources.usage: Body read: Full HTML table independently links modern names with historical administrations: Lesotho/Basutoland, Botswana/Bechuanaland, Malawi/Nyasaland, Zambia/Northern Rhodesia, Zimbabwe/Southern Rhodesia, Namibia/South West Africa. Colony shorthand for Northern Rhodesia is not adopted.

sources.institution: Colonial Office, UK; University of Illinois digitisation
sources.title: Basutoland annual report 1936
sources.usage: Body read: Primary body pp3–4: Cape annexation 1871; general Cape laws not automatic; gun war 1880–1881; direct imperial rule proclaimed 18 March 1884; Resident/High Commissioner, Council 1903; High Commissioner separated from Union Governor-General 1931.

sources.institution: Colonial Office, UK; University of Illinois digitisation
sources.title: Bechuanaland Protectorate annual report 1936
sources.usage: Body read: Primary body pp2–5 and52–53: protectorate 1885 and jurisdiction orders 1890/1891; Resident Commissioner under High Commissioner; chiefs, district officers and advisory councils. Colonial assessments not adopted as objective regime quality.

sources.title: Northern Rhodesia: 20 March 1924
sources.usage: Body read: Complete ministerial body: Company-to-Crown administration transfer1 April 1924; remains protectorate, not colony annexation; Governor, Executive/Legislative Councils. Previous advisory body not statutory legislature. Initial nomination not projected over all later history.

sources.institution: UK Crown, primary Letters Patent republished by vLex
sources.title: Southern Rhodesia Constitution Letters Patent 1923, amended 1927/1934/1937
sources.usage: Body read: Visible primary body recitals and clauses1–14: responsible-government colony, governor, elected Assembly; upper chamber requires later enabling law. Visible amended compilation is not a full read of unseen executive clauses.

sources.title: Migrated archives seventh-tranche guidance
sources.usage: Body read: PDF p19 body: BSAC charter 1889, Crown annexation 1923, federation 1953–1963, later UDI 1965. Later UDI not projected into earlier snapshots.

sources.title: Federation of Rhodesia and Nyasaland Constitution Order 1953 SI 1953/1199
sources.usage: Body read: Primary body founding and territorial-service sections, articles35–39: three separate territories, federal Governor-General/Prime Minister/Assembly/Executive Council, retained territorial governments. Making date is not full commencement.

sources.institution: National Archives and Records Service of South Africa, Cape Archives
sources.title: Prime Minister, Cape of Good Hope authority record
sources.usage: Body read: Full authority body: responsible government 1872, governor-to-government communication, legislative branches and ministerial records through 1910; exact prime-minister tenures. Earlier occupation chronology not claimed.

sources.institution: National Archives and Records Service of South Africa, Cape Archives
sources.title: Magistrate, Kimberley: gazette-backed authority record
sources.usage: Body read: Body dates Griqualand West incorporation 19 October 1880 under Act39 of 1877 and proclamation 15 October 1880; Kimberley magisterial offices. Act, proclamation and operational annexation dates distinguished.

sources.title: Colonial, consular and foreign services, 6 June 1878
sources.usage: Body read: Debate body cc 1292 ff attests Governor-in-Chief/High Commissioner Sir Bartle Frere and Griqualand West colonial administration amid revolt. One-day attestation; allegations of conduct not adopted as objective findings.

sources.title: Former heads of state, government and Governors-General
sources.usage: Body read: Complete historical body: Union 31 May 1910, Governor-General and prime minister; monarchy until republic 31 May 1961. Smuts/Malan/Strijdom/Verwoerd dated premierships. Incomplete/misprinted 1959 Governor-General entry excluded.

sources.title: History: Union and apartheid
sources.usage: Body read: Historical body: Union 1910 restricted participation; National Party/apartheid 1948. Broad franchise-guarantee/slavery 1838 shorthand and modern legal-history errors excluded.

sources.title: International Status of South West Africa, release 1950/30, 11 July 1950
sources.usage: Body read: Primary Registry body: mandate assumed17 December 1920; League dissolution does not terminate obligations; UN supervision, no compulsory automatic trusteeship or unilateral Union annexation. Full opinion not claimed read.
